data.hypothesis: Retaining the fastest measured sparse-obstacle dispatch should preserve its general performance, while an empty-obstacle closed-form path avoids obstacle storage and inverse-factorial table construction when no cells are blocked.
data.notes: Only the fastest measured archived strategy was retained; the measured wavefront, row-list, and SIMD alternatives were slower and were not combined. No commands were run; the controller should evaluate the complete program and all dispatch paths.
transformations: Sort and deduplicate blocked coordinates, then choose between sparse combinatorial counting and a contiguous one-row DP fallback based on estimated pair work versus grid work.
In the no-obstacle case, compute the central binomial coefficient directly using only the needed factorial products and one modular inverse.
